controls.title: Human user identification and authentication
controls.description: Every person must be identified and prove who they are before reaching any function, whether connecting locally, remotely or over an untrusted network. Where shared or role accounts are unavoidable, compensating measures must still tie actions to individuals.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Stronger Security Levels layer on per-person identification, then multifactor login for connections from untrusted networks (RE 1), and finally multifactor login on every interface (RE 2).
assessment_objectives: Confirm that each person is identified and proves who they are on every access path, local and remote, before any permissions take effect.

controls.title: Software process and device identification and authentication
controls.description: Make software processes and devices prove their identity before they are allowed to connect or exchange data, so only known, approved components take part in control traffic.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Once higher Security Levels are targeted, this device and process authentication must cover every interface rather than only selected ones (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that devices and software processes must authenticate successfully before any session with the system is set up.

controls.title: Account management
controls.description: Let authorized administrators handle every account through its whole life: creating, enabling, changing, suspending and deleting it. Plan explicitly for emergency, service and shared accounts, which operational technology relies on heavily.
controls.supplemental_guidance: At higher Security Levels, accounts should be administered from one unified place across the whole system rather than device by device (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm a documented procedure covers creating, changing, disabling and removing system accounts, and that it is actually followed.

controls.title: Identifier management
controls.description: Manage identifiers for users, groups, roles and system interfaces so each one is unique, is not handed out again carelessly, and is deactivated once it is no longer needed.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at every Security Level; pay particular attention to identifiers tied to departed staff or decommissioned interfaces.
assessment_objectives: Check that each identifier is distinct and is issued, tracked and retired under a controlled process.

controls.title: Authenticator management
controls.description: Look after authenticators such as passwords, tokens, certificates and keys: set their initial values, keep them secret, replace factory defaults at installation, and renew them on a regular schedule.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels expect authenticators to be held or protected in hardware (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm factory default credentials were replaced, that credentials are stored securely, and that they are renewed on schedule.

controls.title: Wireless access management
controls.description: Require every person and device that connects over wireless to be identified and authenticated, and grant wireless access only as policy permits.
controls.supplemental_guidance: At higher Security Levels each wireless device must be uniquely identified and authenticated (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that wireless clients and their users must authenticate and be approved before gaining any access.

controls.title: Strength of password-based authentication
controls.description: When passwords are in use, enforce adjustable strength rules such as minimum length and a mix of character types, tuned to the operating context and any safety limits.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add limits on how long a password may be used (RE 1) and block recycling of earlier passwords (RE 2).
assessment_objectives: Confirm the system itself rejects passwords that fail the configured length and complexity rules.

controls.title: Public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates
controls.description: If public key infrastructure is used, run it according to widely recognized good practice, or source certificates from a provider that does.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies from SL2 upward; review certificate lifetimes, issuance procedures and the trustworthiness of any external issuer.
assessment_objectives: Check that certificates come from a PKI operated to accepted good practice and are tracked through issuance, renewal and revocation.

controls.title: Strength of public key authentication
controls.description: When logging in with public keys, check each certificate is valid and not revoked, confirm the user really holds the matching private key, and link the proven identity to an account.
controls.supplemental_guidance: At the top Security Levels, private keys must be guarded by hardware (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm certificate chains and revocation status are checked and that each authenticated key maps to a specific account.

controls.title: Authenticator feedback
controls.description: Hide what is typed or shown during login so that bystanders or screen observers cannot pick up credentials.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; check operator HMIs and engineering tools as well as standard login screens.
assessment_objectives: Check that passwords and similar secrets are masked on screen while being entered.

controls.title: Unsuccessful login attempts
controls.description: Cap the number of failed login attempts in a row at a configurable value and respond in a defined way, without locking operators out of safety-critical or essential operations.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Any lockout behaviour must be designed so it never blocks the access operators need to keep essential functions running.
assessment_objectives: Confirm the failed-attempt threshold can be set, that a response is triggered when it is reached, and that the response does not endanger availability.

controls.title: System use notification
controls.description: Show an adjustable warning or usage notice before a user signs in, wherever the interface is capable of displaying one.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; the notice text normally comes from legal or organizational policy.
assessment_objectives: Check that a usage notice appears before sign-in on each interface able to display it.

controls.title: Access via untrusted networks
controls.description: Watch and control every route by which someone could reach the system from an untrusted network, and refuse such access unless it has been specifically approved.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels require each such connection to receive explicit approval (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm that connections from untrusted networks are logged, controlled and refused unless specifically permitted.

controls.title: Authorization enforcement
controls.description: Enforce the permissions given to each user and device, following the principles of least privilege and duty separation that match real operational roles.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Enhancements extend enforcement to every interface (RE 1), allow supervisors to override (RE 2), require two-person approval (RE 3) and enforce least privilege (RE 4).
assessment_objectives: Check that every user and device can perform only the actions their assigned permissions allow.

controls.title: Wireless use control
controls.description: Approve, watch and restrict how wireless connections are used across the system, in line with the organization's documented policy.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; complements the wireless authentication requirement covering who may connect.
assessment_objectives: Confirm that wireless use is approved, limited by policy and monitored.

controls.title: Use control for portable and mobile devices
controls.description: Automatically apply configurable limits on laptops, phones, USB drives and other portable or removable media when they are connected to the system.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; technical enforcement is preferred over relying on procedure alone.
assessment_objectives: Check that technical limits on portable devices and removable media are applied automatically when they connect.

controls.title: Mobile code
controls.description: Restrict mobile code: decide which mobile code technologies are allowed and stop any unapproved mobile code from running.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels also require the integrity of mobile code to be checked before it runs (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm only approved mobile code technologies are permitted and that unapproved code is prevented from running.

controls.title: Session lock
controls.description: Lock a session after a set idle time or when the user asks, and keep it locked until the user signs in again.
controls.supplemental_guidance: A session lock must never take away the situational awareness an operator needs to run the process safely.
assessment_objectives: Check that the idle timeout can be adjusted and that locking does not hinder safe operation of the process.

controls.title: Remote session termination
controls.description: End remote sessions automatically after an adjustable idle period, or immediately when someone chooses to end them.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies from SL2 upward; idle timeouts should be tuned to how remote support is actually performed.
assessment_objectives: Confirm remote sessions close after the configured idle time and can also be ended on demand.

controls.title: Concurrent session control
controls.description: Restrict how many sessions a single user may have open at once on each interface, using an adjustable cap.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies only at SL3 and SL4.
assessment_objectives: Check that a per-user, per-interface limit on simultaneous sessions is configured and enforced.

controls.title: Auditable events
controls.description: Record security-relevant events, such as access decisions, request errors, system events, backups and restores, and configuration changes, with enough detail for later investigation.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels call for a single audit trail managed centrally across the whole system (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm security-relevant events are logged and that each record holds enough detail to investigate an incident.

controls.title: Audit storage capacity
controls.description: Reserve enough storage for audit records and include measures that make it unlikely the space will run out.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add an alert when storage use passes a set threshold (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that enough space is allocated for audit records and that it is managed so none are lost as it fills.

controls.title: Response to audit processing failures
controls.description: If audit processing fails, notify staff and carry out predefined actions, without disrupting essential operations.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; the defined response must favour keeping the process running.
assessment_objectives: Confirm an audit failure raises an alert and triggers a defined response that keeps essential functions available.

controls.title: Timestamps
controls.description: Stamp audit records with the time, and allow clocks to be synchronized against a common time source for the whole system.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add protection of the time source's integrity and internal clock synchronization (RE 1, RE 2).
assessment_objectives: Check that audit records carry timestamps drawn from synchronized clocks.

controls.title: Non-repudiation
controls.description: Make it possible to prove which user carried out a specific action, so nobody can credibly deny it afterwards.
controls.supplemental_guidance: At the highest Security Level, this must cover every user (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm that actions can be traced to an individual user in a way that holds up if the user disputes them.

controls.title: Communication integrity
controls.description: Protect data in transit against tampering and be able to spot any unauthorized change made while it travels across the network.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels require cryptographic mechanisms to protect integrity (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that data in transit is integrity-protected and that any tampering would be detected.

controls.title: Malicious code protection
controls.description: Put defences in place to prevent, detect, report and contain malware where data enters and leaves the system and on individual components wherever that can be done without disrupting operations.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels require these defences to be centrally managed (RE 1); where antivirus cannot run, use application allowlisting or other compensating measures.
assessment_objectives: Confirm anti-malware measures are installed and managed across the system, with compensating measures where antivirus is not feasible.

controls.title: Security functionality verification
controls.description: Allow security functions to be tested to confirm they work as intended, flagging any failure, either during planned maintenance or at set intervals.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add automated testing (RE 1) and testing while the system is running normally (RE 2).
assessment_objectives: Check that there is a way to test each security function and that any test failure is reported.

controls.title: Software and information integrity
controls.description: Spot, log, report and block any unapproved modification of programs, configurations and other data stored on the system, so tampering does not go unnoticed.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add automatic alerts when an integrity violation is found (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm that unauthorized changes to stored software or data are detected and reported.

controls.title: Input validation
controls.description: Check both the format and the content of any input that can influence control functions, and reject or safely deal with anything malformed.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; cover operator entries, protocol messages and data received from other systems.
assessment_objectives: Check that inputs able to affect control actions are validated for format and content.

controls.title: Deterministic output
controls.description: Drive outputs to a predefined safe state whenever an attack makes it impossible to keep operating normally.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; the chosen safe state should be agreed with process and safety engineers.
assessment_objectives: Confirm outputs move to a documented safe state when normal operation fails or is under attack.

controls.title: Error handling
controls.description: Detect and deal with error conditions in a way that keeps operations going and does not hand attackers useful details.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Error messages should never expose sensitive internal details to people who are not authorized to see them.
assessment_objectives: Check that error handling does not reveal information an attacker could use.

controls.title: Session integrity
controls.description: Keep sessions trustworthy: cancel session identifiers when users log out and refuse identifiers that are forged or replayed.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels require unique, sufficiently random session identifiers (RE 1, RE 2).
assessment_objectives: Confirm session identifiers are protected, cancelled at logout, and rejected when forged or reused.

controls.title: Protection of audit information
controls.description: Guard audit records and the tools used to review them against unauthorized viewing, alteration or deletion.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels expect audit records to be kept on write-once or similarly protected storage (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that audit data and audit tools cannot be altered or removed without authorization.

controls.title: Information confidentiality
controls.description: Keep sensitive information confidential whether stored or in transit, according to how it is classified and the harm its disclosure would cause.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels require encryption both for stored data and for data in transit (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm sensitive information is shielded from unauthorized disclosure both when stored and when transmitted.

controls.title: Information persistence
controls.description: Provide a way to wipe information from shared or reused resources so leftover data is never exposed to unauthorized people.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add confirmation that erasure actually succeeded (RE 1, RE 2).
assessment_objectives: Check that sensitive leftover data is wiped from resources before they are reused or released.

controls.title: Use of cryptography
controls.description: Wherever cryptography is applied, choose algorithms, key lengths and key handling that follow widely accepted industry practice.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; revisit choices as algorithms are deprecated over time.
assessment_objectives: Confirm algorithms, key lengths and key handling match recognized industry guidance.

controls.title: Network segmentation
controls.description: Divide the network logically and physically into zones linked by conduits so data flows are restricted and control networks are kept apart from business networks.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add, in turn, physically independent networking (RE 1), separation from non-control networks such as business IT (RE 2), and separation between distinct control networks (RE 3).
assessment_objectives: Check that the network is split into zones and conduits with restricted data flows between them.

controls.title: Zone boundary protection
controls.description: Monitor and govern traffic crossing zone boundaries so the separation required by the zone and conduit design, which is driven by risk, is upheld.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add deny-by-default rules (RE 1), the ability to isolate a zone in island mode (RE 2) and failing closed (RE 3).
assessment_objectives: Confirm that every zone boundary is enforced at a controlled point where traffic is monitored.

controls.title: General purpose person-to-person communication restrictions
controls.description: Stop everyday person-to-person messaging, such as email or chat, from reaching or leaving control system components unless it has been specifically approved.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; any approved exception should be documented and narrowly scoped.
assessment_objectives: Check that email, chat and similar messaging are blocked to and from control components unless explicitly approved.

controls.title: Application partitioning
controls.description: Allow data, applications and services to be separated according to how critical they are, making zoning and restricted data flows easier.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies from SL2 upward; virtualization or separate hosts are common ways to achieve the separation.
assessment_objectives: Confirm critical applications and services are separated in a way that supports the zone model.

controls.title: Audit log accessibility
controls.description: Give authorized users read-only access to audit logs so security events can be spotted and acted on quickly.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add access to audit logs through a programmatic interface (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that authorized staff can view audit logs, read-only, to support incident response.

controls.title: Continuous monitoring
controls.description: Monitor security mechanisms, network traffic and the operating environment on an ongoing basis so breaches are detected, understood and reported promptly.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels expect ongoing monitoring at every zone and conduit boundary, typically with intrusion detection.
assessment_objectives: Confirm ongoing monitoring is in place and that it detects and reports security events promptly.

controls.title: Denial of service protection
controls.description: Keep essential functions available, even at reduced capacity, while the system is under a denial-of-service attack, and prevent resources from being used up.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add control of communication load (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that essential functions keep working, at least in degraded form, while under denial-of-service conditions.

controls.title: Resource management
controls.description: Cap the resources that security functions may consume so they can never starve essential operations.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; validate this during load testing alongside security tooling.
assessment_objectives: Confirm that security tools are limited so they cannot exhaust resources needed by essential functions.

controls.title: Control system backup
controls.description: Allow user and system data, including configurations and application software, to be backed up without interrupting normal operations.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add checks that backups are intact and usable (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that system data, configurations and software are backed up without disturbing operations.

controls.title: Control system recovery and reconstitution
controls.description: Make it possible to restore and rebuild the system so it returns to a trusted, secure configuration following an outage or fault.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; recovery procedures should be rehearsed, not only documented.
assessment_objectives: Confirm the system can be brought back to a known secure state after an outage.

controls.title: Emergency power
controls.description: Move onto backup or emergency power, and back again, while keeping the security posture unchanged and essential functions running.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; test security settings after real or simulated power transfers.
assessment_objectives: Check that moving to or from backup power leaves security settings and essential functions intact.

controls.title: Network and security configuration settings
controls.description: Allow the system to be configured with the network and security settings that are recommended, and show how its present settings compare with the approved configuration.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add machine-readable reports of the current settings (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm settings match an approved secure baseline and that any drift can be reported.

controls.title: Least functionality
controls.description: Configure the system to offer only the capabilities it truly needs, turning off or restricting unused functions, ports, protocols and services.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at all Security Levels; record a justification for each service left enabled.
assessment_objectives: Check that unneeded functions, ports, protocols and services are turned off or restricted.

controls.title: Control system component inventory
controls.description: Be able to report an up-to-date list of hardware, firmware and software components to support configuration management and tracking of vulnerabilities.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies from SL2 upward; the inventory feeds patching and vulnerability response.
assessment_objectives: Confirm an accurate, current list of components can be generated from the system.

controls.title: Software application - mobile code
controls.description: A software application must limit mobile code within its own runtime, allowing only approved technologies and checking the code's integrity before it runs.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the software-application counterpart of system requirement SR 2.4.
assessment_objectives: Check that the application restricts mobile code technologies and checks integrity before running code.

controls.title: Software application - protection from malicious code
controls.description: A software application must provide, or work alongside, malware protection that suits the host it is installed on.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the software-application counterpart of system requirement SR 3.2.
assessment_objectives: Confirm the application includes or is compatible with malware protection on its host.

controls.title: Embedded device - mobile code
controls.description: An embedded device must allow only approved mobile code technologies to run and check the code's integrity, within the limits of its constrained runtime.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the embedded-device counterpart of system requirement SR 2.4.
assessment_objectives: Check that the embedded device restricts mobile code and checks its integrity.

controls.title: Embedded device - use of physical diagnostic and test interfaces
controls.description: An embedded device must stop its physical diagnostic and test ports, such as JTAG headers or debug interfaces, from being used without authorization.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add active monitoring of whenever these ports are used (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm physical debug and test ports on embedded devices are disabled, locked or otherwise protected.

controls.title: Embedded device - protection from malicious code
controls.description: An embedded device must defend against malware using methods that fit embedded platforms, such as signed code and restricted execution, where traditional antivirus cannot run.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the embedded-device counterpart of system requirement SR 3.2.
assessment_objectives: Check that the embedded device uses suitable malware defences such as code signing or execution control.

controls.title: Embedded device - support for updates
controls.description: An embedded device must accept firmware and software updates securely, checking that each update is genuine and unaltered before installing it.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add verification of update authenticity and integrity (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm embedded devices accept only updates that pass authenticity and integrity checks.

controls.title: Embedded device - physical tamper resistance and detection
controls.description: An embedded device must resist physical tampering, detect it, or both, so that someone with hands-on access cannot quietly manipulate it.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add reporting when tampering is detected (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that embedded devices resist physical tampering or detect when it happens.

controls.title: Embedded device - provisioning product supplier roots of trust
controls.description: An embedded device must allow the manufacturer's roots of trust to be installed and kept safe, so they can be used to validate firmware and device identity.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at SL3 and SL4; confirm how the supplier installs and protects these trust anchors during manufacturing.
assessment_objectives: Confirm the supplier's roots of trust are installed on the device and protected from change.

controls.title: Embedded device - provisioning asset owner roots of trust
controls.description: An embedded device must let the asset owner install and protect their own roots of trust, so they can set trust anchors independently of the supplier.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at SL3 and SL4; useful where owners run their own PKI.
assessment_objectives: Check that the asset owner can install their own roots of trust and that these are protected.

controls.title: Embedded device - integrity of the boot process
controls.description: An embedded device must check that its firmware and software are genuine and unaltered while booting, and respond in a defined way if the check fails.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add an authenticity check on the boot sequence (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm the embedded device enforces secure boot and handles failed verification as defined.

controls.title: Host device - mobile code
controls.description: A host device must allow only approved mobile code technologies and check the code's integrity before letting it run.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the host-device counterpart of system requirement SR 2.4.
assessment_objectives: Check that the host device restricts mobile code and checks its integrity.

controls.title: Host device - use of physical diagnostic and test interfaces
controls.description: A host device must prevent unauthorized use of its physical diagnostic and test ports, such as debug headers or maintenance connectors.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add active monitoring of whenever these ports are used (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm physical debug and test ports on host devices are disabled, locked or otherwise protected.

controls.title: Host device - protection from malicious code
controls.description: A host device must defend against malware, usually through managed anti-malware software or application allowlisting.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the host-device counterpart of system requirement SR 3.2.
assessment_objectives: Check that the host device runs managed anti-malware or allowlisting protection.

controls.title: Host device - support for updates
controls.description: A host device must install operating system and software updates securely, confirming each update is authentic and unaltered.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add verification of update authenticity and integrity (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm host devices accept only updates that pass authenticity and integrity checks.

controls.title: Host device - physical tamper resistance and detection
controls.description: A host device must resist or detect physical tampering to a degree that fits where it is installed.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add reporting when tampering is detected (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Check that host devices resist physical tampering or detect when it happens.

controls.title: Host device - provisioning product supplier roots of trust
controls.description: A host device must allow the manufacturer's roots of trust to be installed and kept safe from alteration.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at SL3 and SL4; confirm how the supplier installs and protects these trust anchors.
assessment_objectives: Confirm the supplier's roots of trust are installed on host devices and protected from change.

controls.title: Host device - provisioning asset owner roots of trust
controls.description: A host device must let the asset owner install their own roots of trust and keep them protected.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at SL3 and SL4; useful where owners run their own PKI.
assessment_objectives: Check that the asset owner can install their own roots of trust on host devices.

controls.title: Host device - integrity of the boot process
controls.description: A host device must check that its software is genuine and unaltered while booting, for example through secure or measured boot, and respond if the check fails.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add an authenticity check on the boot sequence (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm the host device enforces secure boot and responds when verification fails.

controls.title: Network device - wireless access management
controls.description: A network device that offers wireless access must identify and authenticate the people and devices connecting, and allow only approved access.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the network-device counterpart of system requirement SR 1.6.
assessment_objectives: Check that wireless network equipment authenticates users and devices before granting access.

controls.title: Network device - access via untrusted networks
controls.description: A network device must watch and control connections arriving from untrusted networks, refusing them unless they have been specifically approved.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels require each such connection to receive explicit approval (RE 1); this is the network-device counterpart of SR 1.13.
assessment_objectives: Confirm the network device controls and refuses unapproved access from untrusted networks.

controls.title: Network device - mobile code
controls.description: A network device must allow only approved mobile code technologies and check the code's integrity before it runs.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the network-device counterpart of system requirement SR 2.4.
assessment_objectives: Check that the network device restricts mobile code and checks its integrity.

controls.title: Network device - use of physical diagnostic and test interfaces
controls.description: A network device must prevent unauthorized use of its physical diagnostic and test ports, such as console or debug connectors.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add active monitoring of whenever these ports are used (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm physical debug and test ports on network devices are disabled, locked or otherwise protected.

controls.title: Network device - protection from malicious code
controls.description: A network device must defend against malware in ways that suit its role, such as enforcing firmware integrity and restricting what can execute.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the network-device counterpart of system requirement SR 3.2.
assessment_objectives: Check that the network device uses suitable malware defences such as firmware integrity enforcement.

controls.title: Network device - support for updates
controls.description: A network device must install firmware and software updates securely, confirming each update is authentic and unaltered.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add verification of update authenticity and integrity (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm network devices accept only updates that pass authenticity and integrity checks.

controls.title: Network device - provisioning product supplier roots of trust
controls.description: A network device must allow the manufacturer's roots of trust to be installed and kept safe from alteration.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at SL3 and SL4; confirm how the supplier installs and protects these trust anchors.
assessment_objectives: Confirm the supplier's roots of trust are installed on network devices and protected from change.

controls.title: Network device - provisioning asset owner roots of trust
controls.description: A network device must let the asset owner install their own roots of trust and keep them protected.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Applies at SL3 and SL4; useful where owners run their own PKI.
assessment_objectives: Check that the asset owner can install their own roots of trust on network devices.

controls.title: Network device - integrity of the boot process
controls.description: A network device must check that its firmware is genuine and unaltered while booting, and respond in a defined way if the check fails.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add an authenticity check on the boot sequence (RE 1).
assessment_objectives: Confirm the network device enforces secure boot and handles failed verification as defined.

controls.title: Network device - zone boundary protection
controls.description: A network device sitting on a zone boundary must monitor and govern traffic, supporting deny-by-default rules and failing closed, so zone and conduit separation holds.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Higher Security Levels add deny-by-default rules (RE 1), failing closed (RE 3) and an island-mode capability (RE 2); this is the network-device counterpart of SR 5.2.
assessment_objectives: Check that boundary network equipment enforces the zone and conduit rules.

controls.title: Network device - general purpose person-to-person communication restrictions
controls.description: A network device must be able to block email, chat and other everyday person-to-person messages travelling between control system components and other networks.
controls.supplemental_guidance: This is the network-device counterpart of system requirement SR 5.3.
assessment_objectives: Confirm network equipment can block email, chat and similar messaging traffic to control components.
